original_question: Is an arbitrary product of co-sober spaces again co-sober?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Question 9.8: "Is the product space of an arbitrary family of co-sober spaces co-sober?" This is posed immediately after the two-factor special case, Question 9.7. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the correct open problem and gets its scope essentially right: it asks about preservation of co-sobriety under arbitrary products, which is exactly the paper’s Question 9.8 rather than only the two-space case in Question 9.7. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
missing_details: The paper states the problem as a question about the product space of an arbitrary family {X_i}_{i∈I} of co-sober spaces, so the family notation and the use of the product topology should be made explicit. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

To make the question stand-alone, the definition of co-sober must be included: a T0 space X is co-sober if every k-irreducible compact saturated subset K of X is of the form ↑x for a unique x∈X. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The term k-irreducible is implicit in the draft but essential in the paper: G∈K(X) is k-irreducible iff whenever G=K1∪K2 with K1,K2∈K(X), then G=K1 or G=K2. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The notation K(X) is paper-specific and denotes the nonempty compact saturated subsets of X; saturated means upper with respect to the specialization order. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The notation ↑x should be identified as the principal saturated set of x with respect to the specialization order. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The paper works in Top0/with T0 spaces throughout this discussion, which is implicit in the draft because co-sobriety is only defined there. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: Let {X_i}_{i∈I} be an arbitrary family of T0 spaces, and assume that each X_i is co-sober, meaning that every k-irreducible nonempty compact saturated subset K of X_i (equivalently, every K∈K-Irr(X_i)) is of the form ↑x for a unique point x∈X_i, where ↑x is taken with respect to the specialization order. Must the product space ∏_{i∈I} X_i, endowed with the product topology, also be co-sober? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: The draft most directly matches Question 9.8 in Section 9. The paper first asks the binary-product version in Question 9.7 and then says, "More generally, we pose the following," before stating Question 9.8, so the intended target is specifically the arbitrary-family product problem for co-sober spaces, not a broader neighboring issue. The nearby context needed to make the question self-contained is Definition 9.1, which defines k-irreducible compact saturated sets and co-sober spaces, together with the Section 2 notation K(X) for nonempty compact saturated subsets and the use of the specialization order for ↑x. Theorems 9.2 and 9.3 provide adjacent closure facts about co-sober spaces and Smyth power spaces, but the paper does not state any equivalence for Question 9.8 itself. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
